question: Where can I get a list of desalination plants in the United States, with location, capacity, technology, operator and status?

answer.summary: No current national list of desalination plants was found. Reclamation's 2018 survey (Report 207) counts 406 municipal plants of 0.025 mgd or more and details 58 to 84 of them with owner, technology, start year and design and average production in mgd, but no coordinates, no status and no industrial plants. Texas (TWDB, 60 operating plants in August 2024) and California (2019 maps of 12 existing and 6 proposed seawater facilities) add state views, and operators such as Tampa Bay Water publish plant status. Capacity is stated as design, permitted, average or deliverable depending on the source.
main_caveats: Reclamation's inventory is municipal only and dated December 2018: 406 plants are counted but per-plant files cover 84 (TX, FL, CA built since 2010) and 58 summaries.
Reclamation mixes design, permitted and average capacity and does not flag closed plants; it has no coordinates and no status field.
Capacity is not one measure: Carlsbad shows design 54 mgd and average 50 mgd; Tampa Bay Water states up to 12 mgd at restart and 20 mgd when complete.
Texas's database lists operating public-water-supply plants above 0.025 mgd only; its web application could not be opened because TLS verification failed.
California's seawater maps are from 2019 and also name power-plant, aquarium and oil-facility sites besides municipal plants.
Industrial and brackish plants outside Texas, Florida and California were not covered by any per-plant source found.
answer.confidence_reason: Four official or operator sources read with counts and a Carlsbad cross-check; no current national plant list and several sources unreadable or dated.

attributes.note: Reclamation gives city or county only; California's 2019 maps give map symbols; no coordinates found. Texas viewer not readable.
attributes.gap_note: No coordinates were found in the sources opened. TWDB's web application failed TLS verification and was not read, and Florida's state registers and OpenEI files were not opened.

attributes.note: Design and average production in mgd for 47 and 27 of 58 Reclamation summaries; Texas totals 172 mgd for 60 plants; Tampa Bay Water states 12 to 20 mgd. Measures differ.
attributes.gap_note: Capacities are design, permitted, average or deliverable depending on the source; Reclamation says its totals mix them. Per-plant Texas records, California and other states' registers were not read.

attributes.note: Reclamation summaries name the process for 57 of 58 plants (RO 40, NF 9, MF/RO 3, UF/RO 2, others 3); no per-plant technology for the other plants of the 406.
attributes.gap_note: The 406-plant database is described but only plants built since 2010 are detailed in files found. Texas and California registers were not read for process type.

attributes.note: Reclamation gives the facility owner for 55 of 58 plants; Tampa Bay Water names its operating partner. Owner is not always operator.
attributes.gap_note: No dedicated operator field was found; owners and operators may differ. Other operators and state registers were not checked.

attributes.note: Existing vs proposed only in California's 2019 maps; Reclamation gives a start year but no status; Tampa Bay Water posted an outage and restart in 2024.
attributes.gap_note: Reclamation notes that some older plants have closed without flagging them. Current construction or planned stages were not checked, and the Texas database lists operating plants only.

sources.name: Updated and Extended Survey of U.S. Municipal Desalination Plants (Report 207) with Appendices A and B
sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Desalination and Water Purification Research Program (survey by Mickley & Associates)
sources.format: PDF report (56 pages), PDF Appendix B (89 pages) and XLSX Appendix A
sources.summary: Reclamation's 2018 survey of U.S. municipal desalination plants, with per-plant owner, technology, start year and design and average production in mgd for the plants it details.
sources.coverage_note: Municipal plants only; 406 plants counted in 35 states, but per-plant files cover 84 (TX, FL, CA built since 2010) and 58 summaries. No coordinates or status.
caveats: Design, permitted and average capacities are mixed.
Closed plants are not flagged; industrial plants are excluded.

problems: records_total counts plant rows in Appendix A (84); the 406-plant database itself was not found as a file.
report207appendixA.pdf answers 300 (the file is an XLSX); report207appendixC.pdf answers 404.
Counts of design and average production in Appendix B come from text extraction of the PDF.

example.example_request: https://www.usbr.gov/research/dwpr/reportpdfs/report207appendixB.pdf  (entry 'Claude Bud Lewis Carlsbad Desalination Plant, CA')
example.example_result: Owner Poseidon Water; purpose drinking water; technology reverse osmosis; start 2015; RO design production 54 mgd; average production 50 mgd; source water seawater from power plant cooling water.

sources.name: TWDB Desalination Plant Database and Biennial Desalination Report
sources.format: Web application and map viewer; PDF capacity-range map; PDF biennial report
sources.summary: Texas's state database and 2024 biennial report cover public-water-supply desalination plants above 0.025 mgd with design capacity.
sources.coverage_note: Texas only: 60 operating municipal plants, about 172 mgd design capacity (August 2024). The web application could not be opened here.

problems: The web application at www3.twdb.texas.gov failed TLS verification from this environment ('unable to get local issuer certificate'); verification was not bypassed, so plant records were not read.
records_total (60) comes from the 2024 biennial report, not from the application.

sources.name: State Water Board maps of existing and proposed seawater desalination facilities
sources.publisher: California State Water Resources Control Board
sources.summary: California's State Water Board publishes maps listing existing and proposed seawater desalination facilities.
sources.coverage_note: California seawater only; 12 existing and 6 proposed names in 2019 maps; no coordinates, tables or capacity for existing plants.

problems: Capacity per existing plant is not in the PDF text layer; only the proposed map has a capacity legend.

sources.name: Tampa Bay Water: Tampa Bay Seawater Desalination Plant update
sources.publisher: Tampa Bay Water (regional wholesale water utility, Florida)
sources.summary: Operator update on the Tampa Bay seawater plant: status, restart and deliverable capacity in 2024.
sources.coverage_note: One plant, September 2024; current status not confirmed.
caveats: Two years old on the check date.

problems: The operator's desalination-plant page redirects to this blog post; a current status page was not found.

if_unstructured.summary: Plant-level facts sit in PDFs: Reclamation Appendix B facility summaries and operator or state reports.

local_terms.meaning: Reverse osmosis; seawater and brackish-water variants.
Nanofiltration used for softening or contaminant removal.
Groundwater with 1,000 to 10,000 mg/l total dissolved solids (TWDB definition).

provenance.note: Minutes are researcher estimates. Counts describe documented passes, not publication approval. Missing history or effort is not reconstructed.
